newsitem.title: USA: Texas Rangers hold seven men linked to separatists.
newsitem.headline: Texas Rangers hold seven men linked to separatists.

text.p: Seven men reportedly en route to join an armed Texas separatist group holed up in a mountain compound were arrested Wednesday by Texas Rangers, a police spokeswoman said.

The men were arrested at a truck stop in Pecos, Texas, and were found to be carrying fully automatic weapons in their two cars, Texas Department of Public Safety spokeswoman Sherri Deatherage Green said.

The Pecos Enterprise newspaper, quoting unidentified sources, said police in the area, about 70 miles north of Fort Davis in the rugged mountains of west Texas, had been told to be on the lookout for the men.
The DPS said a bulletin had been issued Tuesday warning that three men from a California-based militia might be headed to Fort Davis but it was not clear if these were the same men.

Deatherage Green said she did not know if the men had links to the Republic of Texas group, which has been surrounded by police at its compound in the Davis Mountains since taking, then releasing, two hostages Sunday.

The group advocates the secession of Texas from the United States and has links to anti-government militias. Republic leader Richard McLaren predicted that militia members from around the nation would come to his aid in the standoff.

Deatherage Green said the Rangers arrested the men after Pecos police reported seeing "a suspicious vehicle at a truck stop." She said one of the suspects was wanted on another criminal charge but she did not know what this was.

An employee at the truck stop told reporters the Rangers "handcuffed and laid them out on the sidewalk" when they arrested the men. "They made a statement like 'Look out, there's some more coming,'" when a waitress jokingly asked if they were going to Fort Davis to help the Republic of Texas, the employee said.

Police said 13 Republic members were in the mountain compound. On Tuesday, they said negotiations to end the siege were going well, but McLaren, in calls to the media, insisted he would not surrender unless given full diplomatic immunity.
